records.assessment: S168-a A1 links coffee rings to togetherness, A3 recruits the key ring, and A5 recruits the round table into a message for the whole street. S168-b supplies the parallel accumulation of verbal coincidences into one imperative. The old transfer's knocks and squeaking door no longer come from the seeds and never name the grand message. These fields use the circle chain and explicitly declare togetherness, without retaining unrelated door sounds.
records.secondPassAssessment: Compatible with reservations. The proposed opening and response follow S168-single-a A1/A3: coffee rings, returned keys and a round table become evidence that people should stay together. The closing follows A5 by expanding that supposedly settled message to the whole street. This better expresses the exact card's grand, unquestionable message than the original transfer's composing/rehearsing metaphor. The proposed action is consistent illustrative staging, although tracing a circle beside {prop} is not an exact seed action and requires a suitable prop. The challenge preserves the moving-table conflict but omits B4's crucial fact that the table will not fit in the van; consequently, the closing loses the seed's specific evidence of a circle 'refusing to leave.' The amendment primarily represents alternative a; alternative b supplies a distinct phrase/coincidence mechanism culminating in 'Wait for hope,' which these fields do not retain. The original door rhythm, squeak and rehearsal details have been removed consistently. The cardId, fingerprint, seedIds, seedBindingHashes and compiled-pair-draft status remain unchanged; the hashes identify historical originals, not validated amended dialogue bindings. No bespoke pairs or supporting seeds are supplied, so this establishes transfer-body compatibility only, not pair-level interaction quality or integration validation.
